questions.q: What does Snowflake use instead of T-SQL's TOP keyword to limit rows returned?
options: LIMIT, placed at the end of the statement
Snowflake does not support limiting rows at all
FIRST, placed at the start of the statement
ROWCOUNT, set as a session variable before the query
questions.explain: Snowflake has no TOP keyword; LIMIT goes at the end of the SELECT statement instead.

questions.q: In Snowflake, how are unquoted identifiers like TicketId handled, and why does this project name columns TICKET_ID instead?
options: Unquoted identifiers are folded to lowercase automatically
Snowflake requires all identifiers to be wrapped in square brackets, like T-SQL
Unquoted identifiers are folded to uppercase, so columns are named in uppercase to match
Identifier casing has no effect on anything in Snowflake
questions.explain: Snowflake folds unquoted identifiers to uppercase, which is why this project's columns are named TICKET_ID, CREATED_AT, and so on.

questions.q: What is the Snowflake equivalent of T-SQL's GETDATE(), and what does DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', ...) do?
options: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() is the equivalent of GETDATE(); DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', ...) rounds a timestamp down to the first of its month
GETDATE() works identically in both T-SQL and Snowflake
CURRENT_DATE() returns a timestamp with time, identical to GETDATE()
DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', ...) returns only the month name as text
questions.explain: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()/CURRENT_DATE() replace GETDATE(), and DATE_TRUNC rounds a date/timestamp down to the start of the given unit.

questions.q: Why can't a T-SQL WHERE clause filter directly on a window function like ROW_NUMBER()?
options: WHERE can filter on window functions in T-SQL, identically to Snowflake's QUALIFY
WHERE is evaluated before window functions are computed, so T-SQL needs a CTE or subquery to filter on their results
T-SQL does not support window functions at all
Window functions can only be used in the SELECT list, never for filtering, in any SQL dialect
questions.explain: Because WHERE runs before window functions are evaluated, T-SQL needs an extra CTE or subquery layer just to filter on something like ROW_NUMBER().

questions.q: What does Snowflake's QUALIFY clause let you do that T-SQL cannot do directly?
options: Limit the number of rows returned, replacing LIMIT
Automatically deduplicate rows without any ORDER BY
Join two tables without specifying a join condition
Filter rows based on a window function's result without wrapping the query in a CTE or subquery
questions.explain: QUALIFY filters directly on a window function's output, skipping the CTE/subquery T-SQL would otherwise require.
